summary: Code review passed with two Fix-Forward improvements applied directly. All four acceptance criteria are met, implementation is structurally sound, and tests are well-structured. No blocking issues found.

Fix-Forward #1: Removed dead [ObservableProperty] _greeting field from MainWindowViewModel.cs — the generated Greeting property was not bound in any XAML (MainWindow.axaml hardcodes the title as a string literal). Zero behavioral impact.

Fix-Forward #2: Added HorizontalContentAlignment='Stretch' and VerticalContentAlignment='Stretch' to the ContentControl in MainWindow.axaml. Avalonia ContentControl defaults to top-left content alignment; without this, future hosted views (DatabaseConnectorView, MainContentView) would not fill the available grid cell. Non-behavioral for current placeholder but prevents a latent layout bug.

Architecture is clean: ShellViewModel factory pattern is well-abstracted, ViewLocator convention-based resolution is correct, #if DEBUG guards for CycleThemeCommand are appropriate, and the two-constructor (parameterless + DI) pattern on MainContentView follows the established project convention.

comments.note: Removed dead [ObservableProperty] _greeting = 'Welcome to Video Indexer' field from MainWindowViewModel.cs. The CommunityToolkit-generated Greeting property was never bound in MainWindow.axaml (the TextBlock hardcodes Text='Video Indexer'). Dead generated properties add noise to the public surface and create false binding targets. Confirmed 0 references across the entire workspace before removal.

Added HorizontalContentAlignment='Stretch' VerticalContentAlignment='Stretch' to the ContentControl in MainWindow.axaml (Grid.Row=1). Avalonia ContentControl's default content alignment is top-left, not stretch. Without this, when DatabaseConnectorView or any future real view is hosted, it will appear pinned to the top-left corner rather than filling the content area. Build verified clean (0 errors, 0 warnings) after the change.

In MainWindowViewModelTests.cs AC-1 test, the non-Ready sentinel is an anonymous type: (object)new { NonReady = true }. While functionally correct, a named private class (e.g., class SentinelViewModel {}) would make the test's intent more explicit and align with the test file's established style of using named fake classes. Low priority — the test is readable as-is.

[documentation-forward] MainContentViewModel.cs docstring says 'Will be replaced with the real media-indexer view-model in a future milestone.' The README and docs should note this placeholder so future contributors understand it is intentionally empty and expected to be replaced in a later WP.

The Shell.PropertyChanged subscription in MainWindowViewModel (inside #if DEBUG) is never unsubscribed. This is acceptable for the current architecture since MainWindowViewModel and ShellViewModel share the same application lifetime — both are registered as transient/singleton and neither outlives the other. No action required; documented here for future reference if either lifetime changes.
